title: Reverse proxy vs forward proxy
idea: A proxy is a server that passes requests on for someone else. A forward proxy acts for clients; a reverse proxy acts for servers.

analogy.text: A switchboard. Staff calling out show the company's number (forward proxy). Callers ringing in reach a receptionist who routes them (reverse proxy).
analogy.breaks: A switchboard only connects calls; a proxy can also cache, filter and log.

points: Both sit between clients and servers; the difference is whose side they serve.
A forward proxy serves clients, who are usually configured to send requests through it.
A reverse proxy fronts your servers; clients see one address, not the servers behind.
Reverse proxies often balance load, terminate HTTPS, cache or compress for your app.

steps.caption: Users on one network send their requests through a forward proxy.
The forward proxy sends the request out for them. The site normally sees the proxy's address, not the user's.
On the site's side, a reverse proxy answers first. To outsiders, it is the site.
It picks a backend and forwards the request. The client never learns which server answered.
The reply returns along the same path. Either proxy can log it; plain HTTP replies can also be cached.

code.title: Express behind a proxy
code.caption: Your app sits behind a reverse proxy, so it must be told how to find the real client address.

walk.text: Tell Express one reverse proxy sits in front of this app.
`req.ip` now comes from the `X-Forwarded-For` header, not the connection.
Fake the header a reverse proxy sets, using a documentation-range address.
The response shows the client address Express found.

pitfalls: Behind a proxy, `req.ip` is the proxy's address until you set `trust proxy`.
Trust `X-Forwarded-For` only when your own proxy sets it; clients can fake it.
One reverse proxy is itself a single point of failure; plan a redundant pair.

quiz.q: A reverse proxy forwards a request with `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.4`. What is `req.ip`?
quiz.code:
// no trust proxy setting
app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send(req.ip));
quiz.why: By default Express ignores `X-Forwarded-For`, so `req.ip` is whoever connected: the proxy. `trust proxy` changes that.

takeaway: A forward proxy hides clients; a reverse proxy hides your servers.
